correctness.rationale: The polarity factorizes coordinatewise, giving the exact proper-box closure and rank polynomial for every q>=2 and d>=1. Two-atom join ranks recover Hamming distance for q>=3, while q=2 gives a flat diamond. The explicit three-atom configuration violates modularity precisely in the nonbinary multidimensional case. Pair mixing and q-symbol saturation give an iterative basis of width q, and a coordinate line shows no smaller width can work; coordinate witnesses give direct width <=max(q,d) and private-coordinate witnesses force >=d, plus the line forces >=q. Binary and one-coordinate boundary cases are handled separately. The independent incidence-matrix checker agrees on all 2^16 inputs in each of two largest exhaustive cases. Finite checks support but do not establish the general proof.

originality.rationale: The product-of-contranominal-scales box law is covered in substance by existing general cardinal-product theorems and is NOT claimed independently novel. The assessed specialized contribution is exact optimal Horn premise widths for simultaneous one-pass versus iterative inference, the unbounded dimension gap at fixed nonbinary alphabet, and the binary exceptional lattice symmetry. Explicit comparisons with general closure-system direct-basis papers and product-theory papers did not identify a stronger theorem implying these sharp widths. Possible implicit equivalent statements remain a material originality risk.

value.rationale: For a natural Hamming maximum-distance incidence family, the exact optimal unit-Horn premise width stays q with iterative forward chaining yet is max(q,d) for one simultaneous round at q>=3; thus inference semantics have a provable unbounded arity separation as d grows with fixed alphabet. Explicit minimal witnesses and constructive bases make it an exact, nonroutine structural result. The Boolean-to-height-two symmetry and lattice classifications locate the boundary conditions. The already-known general product law alone does not answer the sharp width question. The result is not claimed to optimize number of rules, computational time, or general products.
